```py
# ---------------- auto-repair: extra exports discovered iteratively ----------------
# File format: one "dllname|exportname" per line. Merged by ensure_synth at build time.
EXTRA_EXPORTS_FILE = '/home/z/my-project/scripts/extra_exports.txt'

def load_extra_exports():
    import os
    out = {}
    try:
        with open(EXTRA_EXPORTS_FILE) as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if not line or line.startswith('#') or '|' not in line:
                    continue
                dll, name = line.split('|', 1)
                out.setdefault(dll.strip().lower(), []).append(name.strip())
    except FileNotFoundError:
        pass
    return out
```

`09_tools/udp_hook.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
udp_hook.py — capture live ESP frame datagrams (DLL -> loader).
Channel (proven by ProcMon): MuMuNxDevice sends UDP datagrams from
localhost:50092 to localhost:4042; PBC loader recvfrom()s them.
Sizes are record multiples: 2992 (1x0xBB0), 11968 (4x), 14960 (5x).
No focus needed at capture time: start hook, PLAY focused 1-2 min,
stop, send the dump file.

Usage (Administrator, cheat+match running):
  venv/Scripts/python.exe 09_bypass_session4/udp_hook.py <PBC-pid> [seconds]
Output: udp_hook_<ts>.bin (concatenated datagrams) + marker summary.
WARNING: VMP may notice Frida injection and kill the cheat. If it dies
on attach, use ProcMon lengths only (safe, no injection).
"""
import struct
import sys
import time

import frida

JS = """
const calls = {};
function cnt(api) {
  calls[api] = (calls[api] || 0) + 1;
  if (calls[api] % 2000 === 0) send({ev: 'STAT'});
}
function emitBytes(u8, tag) {
  if (u8 && u8.byteLength > 0) send({ev: 'DG', n: u8.byteLength, via: tag}, u8);
}
// overlapped (async) completions via IOCP
const pending = new Map();
function trackOv(ov, bufs, count, tag) {
  if (!ov.isNull()) pending.set(ov.toString(), {bufs, count, tag});
}
function hookFlat(name, tag) {
  try {
    const p = Module.getExportByName('ws2_32.dll', name);
    Interceptor.attach(p, {
      onEnter(args) { this.buf = args[1]; },
      onLeave(ret) {
        const n = ret.toInt32();
        if (n > 0 && n <= 65507) {
          try { emitBytes(this.buf.readByteArray(n), tag); } catch (e) {}
        }
      }
    });
  } catch (e) {}
}
function hookFlatCount(name, dll) {
  try {
    const p = Module.getExportByName(dll || 'ws2_32.dll', name);
    Interceptor.attach(p, {
      onEnter(args) { cnt(name); this.buf = args[1]; },
      onLeave(ret) {
        const n = ret.toInt32();
        if (name === 'recvfrom' || name === 'recv') {
          if (n > 0 && n <= 65507) {
            try { emitBytes(this.buf.readByteArray(n), name); } catch (e) {}
          }
        } else if (name === 'WSARecv' || name === 'WSARecvFrom') {
          // sync path with overlapped==NULL handled by dedicated hooks;
          // count only here
        }
      }
    });
  } catch (e) {}
}
hookFlatCount('recvfrom');
hookFlatCount('recv');
// WSARecv (no From) — sync + async-issue tracking
function hookWSA(name, tag) {
  try {
    const p = Module.getExportByName('ws2_32.dll', name);
    Interceptor.attach(p, {
      onEnter(args) {
        cnt(name);
        // WSARecv(s,bufs,count,outN,flags,ov,comp) | WSARecvFrom has from@5,ov@6
        const isFrom = (name === 'WSARecvFrom');
        this.bufs = args[1]; this.count = args[2].toInt32();
        this.outN = args[3]; this.ov = isFrom ? args[6] : args[5];
        trackOv(this.ov, this.bufs, this.count, tag);
      },
      onLeave(ret) {
        if (ret.toInt32() !== 0 || this.ov.isNull()) {
          // sync-immediate (ret 0, ov NULL) or failed
          if (ret.toInt32() === 0 && this.ov.isNull()) {
            let n = 0;
            try { n = this.outN.readU32(); } catch (e) { return; }
            dumpBufs(this.bufs, this.count, n, tag + '-sync');
          }
          return;
        }
        // async issued; completion via GQCS below
      }
    });
  } catch (e) {}
}
function dumpBufs(bufs, count, n, tag) {
  if (n <= 0 || n > 65507) return;
  try {
    const joined = Memory.alloc(n);
    let total = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < count && total < n; i++) {
      const base = bufs.add(i * 16);
      const blen = base.readU32();
      const bptr = base.add(8).readPointer();
      const take = Math.min(blen, n - total);
      if (take <= 0) break;
      joined.add(total).writeByteArray(bptr.readByteArray(take));
      total += take;
    }
    if (total > 0) emitBytes(joined.readByteArray(total), tag);
  } catch (e) {}
}
hookWSA('WSARecv', 'wsarecv');
hookWSA('WSARecvFrom', 'wsarecvfrom');
// IOCP completion side
try {
  const gqcs = Module.getExportByName('kernel32.dll',
                                      'GetQueuedCompletionStatus');
  Interceptor.attach(gqcs, {
    onEnter(args) { this.ovPtr = args[3]; this.nPtr = args[1]; },
    onLeave(ret) {
      if (ret.toInt32() === 0) return;
      let ov = null, n = 0;
      try {
        ov = this.ovPtr.readPointer();
        if (ov.isNull()) return;
        n = this.nPtr.readU32();
      } catch (e) { return; }
      const rec = pending.get(ov.toString());
      if (!rec) return;
      dumpBufs(rec.bufs, rec.count, n, rec.tag + '-iocp');
    }
  });
} catch (e) {}
// report call counters periodically
setInterval(() => { try { send({ev: 'STAT', calls: calls}); } catch (e) {} },
            15000);
// sockets-as-files path: ReadFile/WriteFile on \Device\Afd handles.
// Record datagrams are exact multiples of 0xBB0 (2992).
const REC_SIZES = new Set([2992, 5984, 8976, 11968, 14960, 17952, 20944,
                           23936, 26928, 29920]);
let NtQueryObject = null;
try {
  NtQueryObject = new NativeFunction(
    Module.getExportByName('ntdll.dll', 'NtQueryObject'),
    'int', ['pointer', 'int', 'pointer', 'uint', 'pointer']);
} catch (e) {}
function objectName(h) {
  if (NtQueryObject === null) return '?';
  try {
    const buf = Memory.alloc(1024);
    const st = NtQueryObject(h, 1 /*ObjectNameInformation*/, buf, 1024,
                             ptr(0));
    if (st !== 0) return '?';
    const len = buf.readU16();
    if (len === 0) return '';  // unnamed: socket/Afd/section
    return buf.add(8).readUtf16String(len / 2);
  } catch (e) { return '?'; }
}
function hookFileRW(name, isRead, tag) {
  try {
    const p = Module.getExportByName('kernel32.dll', name);
    Interceptor.attach(p, {
      onEnter(args) {
        cnt(name);
        this.h = args[0]; this.buf = args[1];
        this.want = args[2].toInt32(); this.outN = args[3];
      },
      onLeave(ret) {
        if (ret.toInt32() === 0) return;
        let n = 0;
        try { n = this.outN.readU32(); } catch (e) { return; }
        if (!REC_SIZES.has(n)) return;
        const nm = objectName(this.h);
        if (nm !== '') return;  // real file -> ignore; '' = socket/Afd
        try { emitBytes(this.buf.readByteArray(n), tag); } catch (e) {}
      }
    });
  } catch (e) {}
}
hookFileRW('ReadFile', true, 'readfile');
hookFileRW('WriteFile', false, 'writefile');
// sanity: Sleep MUST fire in any GUI loop (proves agent is alive)
hookFlatCount('Sleep', 'kernel32.dll');
try { send({ev: 'LOADED'}); } catch (e) {}
// lowest level: AFD IOCTLs (catches direct DeviceIoControlFile paths)
const ioCodes = {};
try {
  const dio = Module.getExportByName('ntdll.dll',
                                     'NtDeviceIoControlFile');
  Interceptor.attach(dio, {
    onEnter(args) {
      this.h = args[0]; this.code = args[5].toInt32() >>> 0;
      this.outB = args[8]; this.outL = args[9].toInt32();
      this.ioSt = args[4];
      const k = 'ioctl_' + this.code.toString(16);
      ioCodes[k] = (ioCodes[k] || 0) + 1;
    },
    onLeave(ret) {
      if (ret.toInt32() !== 0) return;
      let n = 0;
      try { n = this.ioSt.add(8).readU32(); } catch (e) { return; }
      if (n <= 0 || n > 65507) return;
      const k = 'ioctl_' + this.code.toString(16) + '_bytes';
      ioCodes[k] = (ioCodes[k] || 0) + n;
      // dump only AFD-ish completions of record-multiple size
      if (REC_SIZES.has(n)) {
        try {
          const nm = objectName(this.h);
          emitBytes(this.outB.readByteArray(n),
                    'ioctl' + this.code.toString(16) + ':' + nm);
        } catch (e) {}
      }
    }
  });
  try { send({ev: 'IOCTL_OK'}); } catch (e) {}
  setInterval(() => {
    try { send({ev: 'STAT', calls: calls, io: ioCodes}); } catch (e) {}
  }, 15000);
} catch (e) {
  try { send({ev: 'IOCTL_FAIL', err: String(e)}); } catch (e2) {}
}
try {
  const wsa = Module.getExportByName('ws2_32.dll', 'WSARecvFrom');
  Interceptor.attach(wsa, {
    onEnter(args) {
      this.bufs = args[1]; this.count = args[2].toInt32();
      this.outN = args[3]; this.ov = args[6];
    },
    onLeave(ret) {
      // sync completion only (overlapped==NULL, ret==0)
      if (ret.toInt32() !== 0 || !this.ov.isNull()) return;
      let n = 0;
      try { n = this.outN.readU32(); } catch (e) { return; }
      if (n <= 0 || n > 65507) return;
      try {
        const joined = Memory.alloc(n);
        let total = 0;
        for (let i = 0; i < this.count && total < n; i++) {
          const base = this.bufs.add(i * 16);
          const blen = base.readU32();
          const bptr = base.add(8).readPointer();
          const take = Math.min(blen, n - total);
          if (take <= 0) break;
          joined.add(total).writeByteArray(bptr.readByteArray(take));
          total += take;
        }
        if (total > 0) emitBytes(joined.readByteArray(total), 'wsarecvfrom');
      } catch (e) {}
    }
  });
} catch (e) {}
"""


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("usage: udp_hook.py <PBC-pid> [seconds=90]")
        return 2
    pid, secs = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 90
    import os
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    ts = time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    path = os.path.join(here, f"udp_hook_{ts}.bin")
    f = open(path, "wb")
    count = [0]
    sizes = {}

    def on_msg(m, d):
        if m["type"] != "send":
            return
        if m["payload"].get("ev") in ("LOADED", "IOCTL_OK",
                                               "IOCTL_FAIL"):
            print(f"[+] {m['payload'].get('ev')}: "
                  f"{m['payload'].get('err', '')}", flush=True)
            return
        if m["payload"].get("ev") == "STAT":
            print(f"[stat] api calls: {m['payload'].get('calls')} "
                  f"io: {m['payload'].get('io')}",
                  flush=True)
            return
        if not d:
            return
        n = m["payload"]["n"]
        via = m["payload"].get("via", "?")
        count[0] += 1
        sizes[(via, n)] = sizes.get((via, n), 0) + 1
        f.write(struct.pack("<I", n))
        f.write(bytes(d))
        if count[0] % 50 == 0:
            print(f"[...] {count[0]} datagrams, sizes={sizes}", flush=True)

    print(f"[*] attaching to PID {pid} ...", flush=True)
    try:
        s = frida.attach(pid)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[!] attach failed: {e}")
        return 1
    script = s.create_script(JS)
    script.on("message", on_msg)
    script.load()
    print(f"[*] hooked recvfrom. PLAY focused for {secs}s ...", flush=True)
    try:
        time.sleep(secs)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    s.detach()
    f.close()
    print(f"[+] {count[0]} datagrams -> {path} sizes={sizes}")
    # quick marker scan of the dump
    blob = open(path, "rb").read()
    off, recs = 0, 0
    marks = {b"FrameStart": 0, b"Matrix": 0, b"player": 0, b"FrameEnd": 0}
    while off + 4 <= len(blob):
        (n,) = struct.unpack_from("<I", blob, off)
        dg = blob[off + 4:off + 4 + n]
        for m in marks:
            marks[m] += dg.count(m)
        recs += 1
        off += 4 + n
    print(f"[+] {recs} datagrams re-scanned, markers={marks}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`09_tools/wpmpush_hook.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""wpmpush_hook.py — prove the push direction (DLL -> loader frames).
Attaches to MuMuNxDevice (ext.dll host), hooks OpenProcess (handle->PID
map) + WriteProcessMemory (target, size). Steady ESP frames show up as
periodic multi-KB writes into the PBC loader PID.
Usage (Administrator, match running):
  venv/Scripts/python.exe 09_bypass_session4/wpmpush_hook.py <MuMuNxDevice-pid> [seconds=60]
"""
import sys
import time
from collections import Counter

import frida

JS = """
const handles = {};
try {
  const op = Module.getExportByName('kernel32.dll', 'OpenProcess');
  Interceptor.attach(op, {
    onEnter(args) { this.pid = args[2].toInt32(); },
    onLeave(ret) {
      if (!ret.isNull()) handles[ret.toString()] = this.pid;
    }
  });
} catch (e) {}
const wpm = Module.getExportByName('kernel32.dll', 'WriteProcessMemory');
const sizes = {};
Interceptor.attach(wpm, {
  onEnter(args) {
    this.h = args[0].toString();
    this.size = args[3].toInt32();
  },
  onLeave(ret) {
    if (ret.toInt32() === 0) return;
    const pid = handles[this.h] || 0;
    send({ev: 'W', pid: pid, size: this.size});
  }
});
setInterval(() => send({ev: 'PING'}), 15000);
"""


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        print("usage: wpmpush_hook.py <MuMuNxDevice-pid> [seconds=60]")
        return 2
    pid = int(sys.argv[1])
    secs = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 60
    by_pid, total = Counter(), [0]
    seen_ping = [False]

    def on_msg(m, d):
        if m["type"] != "send":
            return
        p = m["payload"]
        if p.get("ev") == "PING":
            seen_ping[0] = True
            return
        total[0] += 1
        by_pid[(p.get("pid"), p.get("size"))] += 1
        if total[0] % 200 == 0:
            print(f"[...] {total[0]} writes", flush=True)

    print(f"[*] attaching to PID {pid} ...", flush=True)
    try:
        s = frida.attach(pid)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[!] attach failed: {e}")
        return 1
    script = s.create_script(JS)
    script.on("message", on_msg)
    script.load()
    print(f"[*] hooked WPM. PLAY focused for {secs}s ...", flush=True)
    time.sleep(secs)
    s.detach()
    print(f"[+] {total[0]} WriteProcessMemory calls; agent alive={seen_ping[0]}")
    agg = Counter()
    for (p, sz), c in by_pid.most_common(40):
        print(f"    pid={p} size={sz}: {c}x")
        agg[sz] += c
    print("size histogram top:", agg.most_common(10))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```md
# BestCheatIR CODM Cheat — Full Reverse-Engineering Package

> **Research / educational archive.** Complete binary analysis of a commercial
> Call of Duty: Mobile cheat ("CODM LOADER" by BestCheatIR), including the
> packed sample, fully unpacked images, license-protocol crack, anti-cheat
> bypass documentation, and every methodology used — published because the
> vendor's Telegram channels are repeatedly banned (~weekly) and their mirror
> sites go offline, which would make this sample permanently unavailable to
> future binary-analysis researchers.

- Vendor Telegram (as advertised by the product itself): [t.me/anogs](https://t.me/anogs) · [t.me/pouria_cheat](https://t.me/pouria_cheat)
- Product: "CONTROL CENTER — CODM cheat", compatible with CODM v1.0.57, VMProtect 3.x packed, signed with a **misused Sectigo certificate belonging to MB Oyun Yazilim A.S. (Istanbul, TR)** — reportable to Sectigo.

---

## ⚠️ Safety & legal

- **DO NOT RUN any binary in this repo on your daily system.** See
  [`01_reports/MALWARE_ASSESSMENT.md`](01_reports/MALWARE_ASSESSMENT.md):
  admin-required loader, writes `C:\Windows\System32\ext.dll`, remote-thread
  injection into emulator processes, persistent C2 with cloud kill-switch,
  remote-offset delivery (attacker-controlled payload channel), HWID exfil.
  Every login attempt uploads your HWID to the vendor.
- All samples are provided **as-is for static/dynamic analysis in isolated VMs**
  with snapshots. SHA256 of every binary: [`SHA256SUMS.txt`](SHA256SUMS.txt).
- The loader binary (`02_samples/test.bin`) was purchased legitimately by the
  researcher; this archive exists for preservation and study, not for
  distribution-as-a-product. No license keys are included (redacted).

---

## TL;DR findings

| # | Finding | Details |
|---|---------|---------|
| 1 | **Unpacking** | VMProtect 3.x, 14 protection layers defeated with Unicorn emulation → `.text` 85% / `.rdata` 98% recovered ([METHODOLOGY](01_reports/METHODOLOGY.md) M1) |
| 2 | **License protocol fully cracked** | Request/response both HMAC-SHA256 with the reversed secret; **response signature formula recovered offline** by brute-forcing 8 captured real replies: `HMAC(secret, "true\|LOGIN_SUCCESS\|server_time\|expires_at\|hwid\|nonce")` |
| 3 | **Crash root cause** | The vendor DLL (VMP) silently kills the emulator host process when the login reply is not correctly signed — even with the loader's signature check patched out. Fixing the fake server's signature made everything work **with zero binary patches** |
| 4 | **"Local resolution" myth debunked** | Serving `0x0` for all 16 typeinfo offsets still works — but not via local resolution: the parser uses an **atomic commit** (any failed key ⇒ no globals written ⇒ compiled defaults survive). Works only while defaults match the game build |
| 5 | **Game's custom TypeInfo structure decoded** | `Il2CppClass = *( *( *(TypeInfo+0x58) + 0x78 ) + 0x10 )` (validator `0x18002bb30`); standard `klass->name` reads fail because these are *not* standard Il2CppClass objects |
| 6 | **Architecture** | Loader (overlay/render, ImGui-style menu) ↔ DLL injected into `MuMuNxDevice.exe` (guest memory reads via in-process mapping, camera chain `base+OFF0 → +0x78 → +0x70 → +0x150 → +0xC0 → +0x10 → +0xC0`), pushes 0xBB0-byte records into the loader heap via WPM (push-only IPC, zero loader-side reads — ProcMon-proven) |
| 7 | **Security assessment** | Gray-zone trojan TTPs beyond a usual cheat: see the assessment report; IOC list included |
```
